chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Billy Butterfield and melody players
summary: Maxwell praises Butterfield, Goodman, Armstrong and Ben as jazz melody players.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I'm trying to think of another one. Well, what about Billy, Billy Butterfield?

Well, we worked together in Benny Goodman's band and Billy is one of the most beautiful ballad players I ever heard. He made a record of 'What's New?', when Haggart first wrote it he called it, 'I'm Free.' There was a trumpet solo and I think it ranks right along with Bunny Berrigan's good record of 'Can't Get Started.' But Billy, when he played jazz, bothered me. He would sound good for a while and then he would do what I would think was something trivial, you know, get silly or something. I never liked his jazz playing. But he was probably one of the greatest melody players and to me that's about the highest compliment, because it's the hardest thing in the world to play a good jazz melody. Louis could do it, Bunny Berrigan could do it and he could do it. Well, Hodges didn't play jazz melody, really. He just played a beautiful melody. Ben Webster could play a gorgeous jazz melody, like 'Stepping in a Rocket' (humming.) Hawkins could play a good melody.
Oh, we were just talking about melody players and what a hard thing that is to do.
Oh, yeah, with Billy Butterfield and --

Yeah. You know, Benny Goodman was a good melody player. Something that always interested me, and I used to have a lot of trouble with it, especially when I was young, and I talked to Benny about it. I told him, you know, I thought he was the world's greatest melody player. He was really a good melody player. And he said, no, I'm not the best. He said, Tommy Dorsey's the best, I'm the second best. But I don't like the way Tommy Dorsey played melodies.
You don't like the way Tommy plays?

Well, I certainly admired him as a trombone player, but he was not what I would call a jazz melody player. In fact, to me it sounded like a Mickey Mouse kind of -- awfully good, but it was not what I would call jazz lead, jazz melody. And -- but I always thought that Louis Armstrong was a great jazz melody player, Ben Webster, Coleman Hawkins, Billy, of course, Bunny Berigan. There are not too many of them. Of course, I'm not too sure how interested anyone is in doing that any more.
